claims.text: CALPHAD-guided design improves phase stability, microstructural refinement, and properties relative to design without computational guidance.
HEAs possess a vast compositional design space.
Conventional HEA design routes may produce multiple phases, including undesired intermetallics.
CALPHAD can be combined with physicochemical criteria, data mining, and multi-objective optimization for HEA design.
CALPHAD-based calculations can screen candidate HEA compositions.
CALPHAD-based design can guide processing parameters.
The Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti quinary system is an example of a system amenable to high-throughput CALPHAD screening.
CALPHAD calculations require computational software and a thermodynamic database.
CALPHAD design enhances phase distribution, produces a dominant solid-solution phase, and reduces secondary intermetallic phases.
Reducing secondary intermetallic phases produces a more homogeneous microstructure.
CALPHAD predicts mixing enthalpy, mixing entropy, atomic-size difference, and the omega parameter.
The predicted thermodynamic parameters guide selection of compositions favoring single-phase stability.
CALPHAD predictions inform processing conditions that refine microstructure and optimize mechanical properties.
CALPHAD-designed HEAs will exhibit a single solid-solution phase with fewer secondary phases.
A single solid-solution phase with fewer secondary phases will improve mechanical performance and microstructural homogeneity.
Trial-and-error alloy design often produces mixed-phase structures and less optimized properties.
The benefits of CALPHAD are limited by the accuracy and completeness of the underlying thermodynamic databases.
CALPHAD predictions require additional experimental validation when kinetic factors dominate phase formation.

contradictions.description: The mediator proposes a dominant solid-solution phase with reduced but remaining secondary phases, whereas the outcome calls the material single-phase while simultaneously saying it has fewer secondary phases. A genuinely single-phase alloy cannot contain secondary phases.
